questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Humboldt University due to their academic heritage, having had some of my personal academic idols attend.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Unfortunately I had a very bad time due to a lack of support and understanding from the host university. I would like to highlight that the poor review is 100% about the host university and not about Erasmus+ and the sending university at all.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was practically impossible to get the needed information when I arrived. The host university does not help with any practical stuff whatsoever, causing a great deal of stress already at the start of the semester.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None. I tried to get assistance in regards to sign up for classes, which they could not help me with. Most information found online is outdated and not relevant anymore, causing even more confusion regarding the propper procedures. I tried to get help with how to deal with feeling isolated as an exchange student, which I was told was normal and that I would get over it (I didn't).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There was a single orientation at the start of the semester, which did not deliver any useful information at all. Instead of giving us practical information about how to sign up for things or who to contact with questions, we were walked around one of the four campuses, which ended up being useless due to not having any classes there anyway.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The host university offered me accommodation, however I would not recommend taking it. Instead try looking online for shared apartments with other young people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Berlin is quite large, so make sure to find something thats not too far from public transport.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The accommodation that I was given was horrendous. I had heating for less than 30% of my stay, which sucks since I was there during the winter. We would also go atleast 5-8 days a month without warm water. Sometimes we would also lose access to electricity for days at a time. The person in charge of the building would also threaten other tenants, which caused me to be scared of speaking up if problems arose.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a stressful and horrible experience due to the lack of guidance available.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Since none of the classes I had gotten pre-approval for were available, I was told (after asking for help 3 times) to just show up to class and practically beg for a seat in the class. It took several week to get all the classes I needed due to not being able to sign up for classes online like regular students could. I was treated as a secondary priority, with regular students automatically having higher priority due to being able to sign up for classes online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: None. I asked for help everywhere that I could but did not find any help whatsoever. I ended up just showing up for courses and speaking with the other students and professors in order to get guidance.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: All the classes I had gotten pre-approval for were not available. I ended up having to take whatever I could get, which caused me to take some courses I had no genuine interest in or wasn't academically prepared for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Honestly just go to a different university. If you insist on going to Humboldt, be ready to spend the first few weeks stressing and showing up for 10-15 different classes before getting your final schedule.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I do not feel I learned anything of value during my stay. It felt like there was more of a focus on making sure people remembered specific formulas or quotes rather than how to apply theoretical concepts in a practical setting.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses felt at the same time both horribly simple and boring, but also excruciatingly hard when it comes to exams and homework. There was practically zero student involvement in the actual lectures, so you would just show up to listen to a professor talking for 2 hours with no breaks. Most of my classes also had almost no litterature available to read in order to get ready for exams, so you were stuck with studying badly put together slides.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was much much worse. I am used to learning about theoretical concepts and then being given time to apply them to actual situations, which I like, however at Humboldt it felt like the only things that matter are remembering formulas or quotes. I was thus greatly unprepared for the exams due to the required knowledge was so much different from what I am used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
IT Project Management
Grundlagen Der Programmeirung
Nichtbewusste Kognition
Félix Guattaris Science-Fiction-Filmskript über das Infra-Quark Universium
Dramaturgien des Schrecklichen

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Stick to english courses unless you are fluent in german. IT Project Management was a fun class.

questions.answer: Food was very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was not made aware of any opportunities. I could not find any relevant information online either

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: None that I know of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: You could attend ESN events, however the ones that I did attend seemed more like a private friend group that you are intruding on. Not very inclusive.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The museums in Berlin are great!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Other than the language barriers and the insane amount of bureaucracy, the culture was pretty easy to adjust to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They don't wanna socialize with you. Due to the more free structure, people often don't share the same classes, which means there isn't much socializing going on.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The lack of group work.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, music and art of Berlin is amazing. I also loved going to flea markets.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared to do alot of paperwork.
Be stubborn when the administration doesn't give you the answer you are looking for. 
There are some cool people in Berlin, try to find them!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you are near fluent in german if you wanna take classes in german

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The feeling of indepence (mostly due to the administration at the host university not helping at all)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The bureaucracy and lack of help from the administration. The exam form is also very different, which caused me alot of issues.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Again, this negative review is purely for Humboldt. Do not let my experience discourage you from taking an exchange semester, as it is generally a very rewarding experience.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
